what_it_does: NetCrafter tackles a wiring bottleneck in multi-GPU clusters: GPUs within a group have fat, fast links, but inter-group links are slower. When traffic crosses the slow link, packets often arrive partially filled or contain speculative data not yet needed, wasting bandwidth and increasing latency. NetCrafter applies three techniques at the network boundary: flit stitching (combining partially-filled packets destined for the same place), flit trimming (dropping speculative data not yet requested), and flit sequencing (prioritizing latency-critical packets ahead of bulk data). Together, these raise effective network utilization and reduce end-to-end latency.
